Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller version of the same problem. Each call does a tiny piece of work, then hands the rest off to the next call, until the problem gets so small it can be answered directly — that's called the base case. Once the base case returns a value, each previous call finishes its work and passes the result back up the chain. Think of it like a set of nesting dolls: you keep opening smaller ones until you reach the tiniest one, then put them all back together on the way out.
